s: Separates the command (write) model from the query (read) model, optimizing each independently for its access pattern.
w: Commands mutate state through a write model (normalized DB, event store). Queries read from a denormalized read model (cache, search index, materialized view). A synchronization mechanism (CDC, event bus, polling) keeps read models eventually consistent with writes. This lets you scale reads horizontally via replicas/shards while writes stay strongly consistent, and optimize read shapes per consumer.
use: Read-heavy systems where read and write scaling needs diverge drastically
Complex query patterns that benefit from purpose-built read models per use case
Event-sourced systems needing fast queries without replaying full event streams
Multi-team systems where each team builds their own read projection
avoid: Simple CRUD where read/write paths are trivially the same
Strong read-after-write consistency requirements without acceptable lag
Small teams who cannot manage the operational complexity of dual models

pat.d: Events stored as log; projections rebuilt from events to serve reads.
Database CDC feeds read models in near-realtime without event store.

pits: Eventual consistency causing user confusion - implement read-your-writes via write confirmation tokens
Projection lag making reads appear stale - monitor lag and expose freshness indicators
tips: CQRS is OPTIONAL complexity - start with single model and introduce when read/write needs genuinely diverge
Eventual consistency is the main challenge - explain how you communicate lag to users
